subject: Linear Algebra
title: Linear Transformations, Eigenvalues and Diagonalization
note: Original ACADRIX practice MCQs based on the R-2025 Unit II syllabus. These are not official Anna University questions or PYQs.

questions.q: A function T: V → W is a linear transformation if it preserves which two operations?
questions.explanation: A linear transformation satisfies T(u+v)=T(u)+T(v) and T(cu)=cT(u).

questions.q: For a linear transformation T, what is T(0)?
questions.explanation: Every linear transformation maps the zero vector of its domain to the zero vector of its codomain.

questions.q: Which condition must hold for a map T to be linear?
questions.explanation: Additivity is one of the two defining properties of a linear transformation.

questions.q: The null space of T consists of all vectors v such that:
questions.explanation: The null space, or kernel, is the set of all domain vectors mapped to the zero vector.

questions.q: The range of a linear transformation T is the set of:
questions.explanation: Range(T)={T(v):v belongs to the domain}.

questions.q: The null space of a linear transformation is a subspace of its:
questions.explanation: The null space contains vectors from the domain that are mapped to zero.

questions.q: The range of T is a subspace of the:
questions.explanation: All outputs of T lie in the codomain, and the range is closed under linear combinations for a linear transformation.

questions.q: If T: R² → R² is given by T(x,y)=(x+y, x-y), then T is:
questions.explanation: Both components are linear combinations of x and y, so the map satisfies linearity.

questions.q: If T: R² → R² is defined by T(x,y)=(x²,y), then T is:
questions.explanation: The x² term violates homogeneity and additivity required for linearity.

questions.q: The dimension of the null space is commonly called the:
questions.explanation: Nullity is the dimension of the kernel or null space.

questions.q: The dimension of the range of a linear transformation is called its:
questions.explanation: Rank is the dimension of the range or image of the transformation.

questions.q: For T: V → W, the dimension theorem relates dimension(V) to:
questions.explanation: The dimension theorem states dim(V)=rank(T)+nullity(T) for a finite-dimensional domain.

questions.q: If dim(V)=6 and nullity(T)=2, then rank(T) is:
questions.explanation: By the dimension theorem, rank + nullity = 6, so rank = 6−2 = 4.

questions.q: The matrix representing a linear transformation depends on the:
questions.explanation: The matrix representation is determined relative to chosen bases for the domain and codomain.

questions.q: For a linear transformation T: Rⁿ → Rᵐ, its standard matrix has dimensions:
questions.explanation: Each of the n domain basis vectors produces a column in Rᵐ, giving an m×n matrix.

questions.q: The columns of the standard matrix of T are obtained by applying T to the:
questions.explanation: The jth column is T(ej), expressed in the codomain basis.

questions.q: An eigenvalue λ of a matrix A satisfies:
questions.explanation: An eigenvalue has a corresponding nonzero eigenvector satisfying Av=λv.

questions.q: A vector associated with an eigenvalue λ is called an eigenvector if it is:
questions.explanation: Eigenvectors must be nonzero vectors satisfying Av=λv.

questions.q: Eigenvalues of A are found from the characteristic equation:
questions.explanation: The characteristic polynomial is det(A−λI), and its roots are the eigenvalues.

questions.q: If A is a 2×2 matrix, its characteristic equation is generally a polynomial of degree:
questions.explanation: An n×n matrix has a characteristic polynomial of degree n, so a 2×2 matrix gives degree 2.

questions.q: For a triangular matrix, the eigenvalues are the:
questions.explanation: The characteristic polynomial of a triangular matrix is the product of λ-adjusted diagonal entries.

questions.q: Eigenvectors corresponding to distinct eigenvalues of a matrix are:
questions.explanation: Eigenvectors associated with distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent.

questions.q: The eigenspace corresponding to λ is the null space of:
questions.explanation: The eigenspace is the set of solutions of (A−λI)v=0.

questions.q: A matrix is diagonalizable if it has enough linearly independent:
questions.explanation: An n×n matrix is diagonalizable when it has n linearly independent eigenvectors.

questions.q: If an n×n matrix has n distinct eigenvalues, it is:
questions.explanation: Distinct eigenvalues provide n linearly independent eigenvectors, which is sufficient for diagonalization.

questions.q: In a diagonalization A=PDP⁻¹, the columns of P are:
questions.explanation: P is formed from a basis of eigenvectors, while D contains the corresponding eigenvalues on its diagonal.

questions.q: In A=PDP⁻¹, the diagonal entries of D are:
questions.explanation: The diagonal matrix D contains the eigenvalues corresponding to the eigenvectors used as columns of P.

questions.q: If 0 is an eigenvalue of A, then A is:
questions.explanation: A matrix with eigenvalue zero has determinant zero and therefore is singular.

questions.q: For an invertible matrix A, which value cannot be an eigenvalue?
questions.explanation: If zero were an eigenvalue, det(A) would be zero, contradicting invertibility.

questions.q: If A is diagonalizable as A=PDP⁻¹, then A and D have the same:
questions.explanation: Similar matrices have the same characteristic polynomial and hence the same eigenvalues.
